Hi team,

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive:

1) Hosted API: currently GA in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Hosted routing is region-aware for inference (i.e., requests can be routed to the EU region), but our public control plane metadata (billing/usage) is still processed in our control plane which is US-based by default. For customers with strict control-plane constraints we recommend Private.

2) Dedicated capacity: we can pin GPU pools to a single region (eu-central-1 / eu-west-1). Network egress can be restricted via VPC peering and strict firewall rules; backups can be configured to remain in-region.

3) Private VPC / On-prem: supports full in-region residency. We offer customer-managed KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM appliance) and can disable any external telemetry for compliance. This is the cleanest option for your PII constraint.

4) Cross-region backups: by default some automated snapshot replication is available for Hosted to improve reliability; that can be turned off for Dedicated/Private with an addendum to the contract.

5) Latency: POC on Hosted EU region typically sees 20-60ms p95 for single-token generation on standard models; Dedicated can reduce variance and get to sub-20ms p95 depending on model/quantization; Private on customer hardware depends on VM size but is similar to Dedicated when properly provisioned.

Attachments: region_capabilities_table.xlsx (XLSX), deployment-options-overview.pdf (PDF)

I'll cover the above in the call and bring a short slide to map cost bands. For NordBank specifically, Private VPC in eu-central-1 with customer KMS and in-region backups is doable. We'll need to align on contractual language about backups and audit log retention.

Cheers,
